hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: Invert every continuous block of length k within the array.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: Advance in strides of k and reverse elements from start to min(start + k - 1, n - 1).

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Use two opposite pointers swapping elements inward until they meet.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def reverseKSubarrays(nums: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    res = list(nums)
    n = len(res)
    for start in range(0, n, k):
        l = start
        r = min(start + k - 1, n - 1)
        while l < r:
            res[l], res[r] = res[r], res[l]
            l += 1
            r -= 1
    return res
```

complexity.notes: Each element is swapped at most once in a single linear pass.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Creating separate array slices repeatedly can introduce extraneous reallocation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Produces a modified copy of the input array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applies standard two-pointer array reversal within bounded windows.
